fatal_errors: The proposed zirconium addition and AlNbTiVZr system are unrelated to the target Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 alloy and its Fe/Co/Mn/P compositional adjustment.
The sole cited paper concerns high-temperature oxidation of crystalline AlNbTiVZr0.25 and supplies no evidence that zirconium enhances glass-forming ability.

A lower crystallization-onset temperature is treated as evidence of improved glass-forming ability, although it generally indicates reduced thermal stability unless supported by separate critical-cooling-rate or critical-thickness data.
The hypothesis misses the target distinction between eutectic-dominated solidification in the modified composition and complete amorphization only in approximately 20 micrometer melt-spun ribbons.
explanation: The response addresses metallic-glass formation only at a generic level. Its size-mismatch and diffusion-suppression rationale is scientifically plausible in some Zr-bearing systems, and the paired-alloy experiment with XRD and critical casting thickness would be discriminating. However, it does not reconstruct the target material, compositional intervention, phosphide/eutectic mechanism, measured cooling conditions, ribbon-only amorphization, or observed devitrification behavior. Most importantly, the cited oxidation study does not validate any glass-formation claim. Thus this is an unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction.
